config_name: OmniBook Ultra 14 — Core Ultra 5 226V, 16GB LPDDR5x, 512GB SSD, 14" 120Hz touch

battery.notes: ~59Wh. Lunar Lake 226V is the most efficient tier of the line; 15h light use plausible.

offers.name: HP OmniBook Ultra 14" 120Hz Touchscreen Laptop - Intel Core Ultra 5 226V - 16GB LPDDR5x - 512GB SSD - Windows 11 - Eclipse Gray

reviews.quote: I Tested HP's OmniBook Ultra 14, a Gorgeous Ultraportable With Potent Processing Power

praises: Lunar Lake 226V gives the best battery life of any OmniBook Ultra tier — 14-15h real use
Near-silent: the efficient chip rarely spins the fan in office work
120Hz smoothness even at 1200p makes scrolling feel premium
Lightest Ultra 14 tier at ~1.34 kg with the same aluminium build
Frequently discounted near $1,500 — HP's premium chassis at midrange money
complaints: 16GB base RAM is the floor of acceptable in 2026 and it is not upgradable
Base panel is 1200p IPS — a big step down from the 3K OLED the line is known for
Ultra 5 226V multicore trails every H-class rival for coding/compile work
Same HP bloatware as the rest of the line

design_philosophy: The efficiency-first entry into HP's premium clamshell line: Lunar Lake's class-leading perf-per-watt in the same shell as the flagship, for road warriors who prioritise battery and silence over raw power.
rating_notes: Inferred from PCMag OmniBook Ultra 14 anchor; base 1200p IPS panel drops screen_quality to 6.5 per dataset IPS convention. Lunar Lake 226V: best battery (9.0), weakest multicore. 47 TOPS NPU keeps ai_ml modest.
